findings.evidence: scripts/build_explorer.py: LINK_DESTINATION_RE accepts an optional `"title"` or `'title'` after the destination. parse_inline only reads `parsed.group(1)` for the destination, so the title never reaches the output. docs/engineering/explorer.md says an unsupported construct inside an included excerpt fails the build and is never dropped. A source link like `[x](a.md "Title")` therefore renders without its title, and no test covers this.
findings.summary: The renderer's fail-closed contract says unsupported constructs are never dropped, but an inline link title is accepted and discarded without an error.

findings.evidence: tests/test_build_explorer.py: `@unittest.skipIf(shutil.which("copier") is None, "copier is not installed")` on test_rendered_new_project_contains_no_explorer_artifact. docs/engineering/explorer.md says the test "renders a project and fails if any Explorer artifact appears". In an environment without copier, this check is skipped rather than failed. That is a degraded path, and the repo's no-fallback rule favours failing explicitly.
findings.summary: The only test that renders a project and checks that no Explorer artifact appears is skipped when `copier` is missing. The skip is silent, and the downstream-boundary requirement is then covered only by static path checks.
